growth_story.headline: Botswana's diamond-led growth has swung hard; after falls in 2024 and 2025, income per person is back about where it first was in 2017.
growth_story.arc: Income per person in Botswana grew 2.7 percent a year in 1990–1999, while diamonds drove the economy. Growth slowed to 0.4 percent a year in 2000–2009, an average dragged down by a fall of 15.9 percent in 2009, when a diamond slump came with the global financial crisis. The 2010–2017 era ran at 3.3 percent a year, helped by the bounce back from 2009, though income per person fell 6.2 percent in 2015 in a year of recession and drought. Since 2018 growth has averaged 0.4 percent: income per person fell 10.0 percent in 2020, rose 10.3 percent in 2021 as diamond sales recovered, peaked in 2023, then fell 4.4 percent in 2024 and 2.3 percent in 2025 as diamond output dropped. It now sits 6.6 percent below that peak, about where it first was in 2017, and the World Bank sees this diamond downturn as structural rather than a passing slump like past ones.

threads.title: A diamond slump that may last
threads.text: Demand for natural diamonds has weakened as lab-grown stones and other suppliers compete, and the World Bank sees diamond revenues as structurally weaker than in past slumps. The IMF tied the 2025 contraction mainly to a further fall in diamond production.

threads.text: Years of weak diamond exports and spending that did not adjust have used up the savings that once cushioned slumps. Public debt has climbed quickly since 2023.

threads.title: Exports still mostly diamonds
threads.text: Despite years of diversification plans, diamonds still make up most exports, much as they did in the early 1990s, with copper and tourism the only other large earners abroad. Unemployment has stayed high.

threads.title: Past slumps were cushioned
threads.text: Diamond downturns during the global financial crisis and in the mid-2010s were sharp but short, and savings built up in boom years absorbed them. That fits the deep falls in 2009 and 2015 and the quick rebounds of 7.8 percent in 2010 and 5.7 percent in 2016.

threads.text: Beyond diamonds, the World Bank lists recession, droughts, floods and COVID-19 as shocks that slowed growth after 2015. A short run of strong diamond revenue after the pandemic, helped by disrupted Russian supply, came as income per person rose to its 2023 peak.

since_last_year.text: The economy shrank for a second year in 2025 as diamond revenues weakened and fiscal pressure grew. By mid-2026 the World Bank reported diamond mining recovering in the first quarter of 2026 and expected growth to return that year.

growth_story.tension: The World Bank describes much faster total GDP growth in the 1990s than the 2.7 percent a year that income per person shows for 1990–1999; the gap is growth spread across a growing population. The 2023 World Bank review also says growth has trended down since 2010, while the data show 2010–2017 as the fastest era at 3.3 percent, an average lifted by the rebound from the 2009 fall and a jump of 9.4 percent in 2013.
